newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-RBA says policy settings allow higher growth.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-RBA says policy settings allow higher growth.

text.p: Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) said on Tuesday current policy settings have scope to accommodate higher economic growth and that continuing low inflation was a sound basis for economic expansion.

In its August bulletin, the central bank said domestic-sourced inflation appears to be in check, wage pressures have eased in recent months and the current level of the Australian dolar implied stability in imported goods prices. The RBA said also monetary policy was providing some expansionary impetus and that higher growth should lead to lower unemployment.

The RBA said also that business confidence was not strong but seemed to be improving and that second quarter demand and output expanasion was likely to be a slower pace than at that seen at the beginning of the year.

"The present setting of policy also embodies a judgement that even if growth in demand turned out to be a little higher than expected, the economy has scope, in the short-term at least, to respond without serious inflation consequences," it said.

"The increasing evidence that low inflation is being maintained -- which is a feature of the business and economic environment globally -- makes for a sound base for economic expansion," the central bank said.
CPI inflation rose 0.3 percent in the year to June, while underlying inflation was 1.7 percent, the lowest since 1971.

"If the exchange rate remains at current levels, it would imply relative stability in prices for imported consumer goods, or even some further small declines over the next few quarters, as a result of the continuing (although diminishing) response to earlier exchange rate appreciation," it said.

The Australian dollar was trading at US$0.7375 on Tuesday afternoon and has fallen from around US$0.8000 in March. The RBA has cut rates five times by 50 basis points each since July 1996. Official cash rates are currently at 5.00 percent.
"Notwithstanding the important contribution of the exchange rate to recent trends, domestically sourced inflation also appears to be in check," it said.
"Wage pressures at an aggregate level have eased in recent months, probably reflecting a period of weaker labour market conditions as well as declines in inflation expectations," it said.
"There are also signs of a slight decline in rates of increase in executive earnings and in wage increases negotiated under enterprise agreements," the RBA said.
"Business confidence, although not strong, seems to have been improving, particularly expectations about future conditions.
"Monetary policy is providing some expansionary impetus: the structure of interest rates for most borrowers is lower now than at the previous low point in 1993, including in 'real' terms," it said.

"As these factors exert their influence over the coming year, further acceleration in growth can be expected to be accompanied by a resumption in employment growth and a further reduction in the rate of unemployment," the RBA said.

The government has forecast growth of 3.75 percent for the year to June 30, 1998. Latest data shows the Australian economy grew just 2.4 percent in the year to March 1997. June quarter GDP data is due on September 3.
Unemployment rose to 8.7 percent in July from 8.5 percent in June and has remained at or above 8.5 perent for moost of the past two years. -- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
